chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who does not want the sweet dishes from us, wants the drinks.

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), referring to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of sharing sweets in Shia etiquette according to the hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) highlights the social nuance of hospitality, suggesting that refusing sweets while accepting drinks implies a subtle distinction in status or preference, as confectionery is traditionally viewed as a superior delicacy. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) in social interactions, where the quality of the gift offered serves as a marker of respect and generosity. The statement underscores the importance of consistency in treating guests equally to avoid unintended signals of partiality.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who does not want (to eat) the sweet dishes from us, wants the (sweet) drinks’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “
If one of us does not want al-Halwa’ he wants drink (which is sweet).”’
